segments.transcript: Your instructions survived almost everywhere, but the plan had drifted in a few spots. The biggest fixes are now baked in. Every safety gate must also prove it does not slow the agents down. That is your not-hindering-actual-usage rule. It was only on one gate before; now it is on all of them. And the gate that counts running agents counts only the ones actually working. An open pane waiting for you costs nothing, exactly as you said. Your you-can-just-do-it on the fleet-law install was found on the record, in your own words, so the law stays installed, and the checker now requires that kind of receipt for every future install. The terminal-manager handoff had quietly dropped three promised improvements; the new lead has them back on its list by name. And the new items you asked for that had no owner now have one: keeping the second Mac perfectly in sync, the language-rewrite research pipeline, and writing down how a new lead takes over. Two decisions need you today. First, the one with a deadline. Your Fable access through the subscription ends around tomorrow; after that it costs usage credits. The question is whether to keep the two top seats on Fable with credits, or drop back to Opus. Tonight, Fable caught several mistakes the Opus-era seats missed, but the discipline systems mattered more than the model, and everything we build stays model-agnostic either way. Second, a one-word check. When you said token-intake-buddy, we think you meant a cheap helper model that reads the huge stuff, big files and screenshots, and hands the smart model a short digest. If that is right, we will build it as a standard pattern. There are also two standing choices at the bottom: how you want to approve the safety gates as they arrive, and whether you will set up Cloudflare this weekend for real dashboard speed. The quick loading fix ships either way. All four are waiting for you in the boxes below.
